mechanism_narrative: A negative change in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an easing monetary cycle that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as the present value of future cash flows increases.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1 percentage points over the past month, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate exceeding 0.2 percentage points over the past three months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit expectations to produce negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises by more than 0.2 percentage points over three months, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) by at least 0.5% over the past month signals an economic contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth expectations to cause negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO and PAYEMS both decline by at least 0.5% over the past month, the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 0.5% over the past month signals weakening consumer demand, reducing real estate sector performance to produce negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines by at least 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, when HOUST declines by at least 0.5% in one month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over the past three months signals accelerating inflation, triggering monetary policy tightening to reduce equity valuations and produce negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.3 percentage points over three months, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A positive change in monthly payroll employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 0.5% over the past month signals strengthening labor market conditions, boosting consumer spending and corporate revenue growth to produce positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% over the past month, the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) by at least 1% over the past month signals a contraction in consumer demand, reducing corporate sales growth expectations to cause negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When RSAFS and HOUST both decline by at least 1% over the past month, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles, a rise in the federal funds rate exceeding 0.25 percentage points over the past month signals aggressive policy tightening, increasing cost of capital to produce negative 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25pp in 1 month
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, when FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.25 percentage points over one month, the 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of cases.
